__comment: Default / clear-day sky master. Loaded by the SkyController autoload.
Trimmed Forward+ equivalent of Stonehearth's data/calendar/sky_settings.json; colour and
height_fog numbers below are seeded directly from Stonehearth's validated sunny settings.
DATA ONLY. Per-frame interpolation between keyframes lives in SkyController.gd. Weather files
(data/weather/*.json) override only the deltas of this base via their 'sky_overrides' block.
Keys beginning with '__' are documentation comments and are skipped by the loader.
KEYFRAME SHAPE: every curve is an array of { "at": <event_name>, ... } points. 'at' must be
one of the event_times in data/calendar/calendar.json. SkyController expands event names to
seconds, sorts, and interpolates; the curve wraps from the last point back to the first.
CELESTIALS (sun, moon): each directional light has:
light_color   [r,g,b] 0-1  - emitted colour; (0,0,0) => light switched OFF (this is how the
sun 'sets' and the moon 'rises'). Also tints the fog (see below).
ambient_color [r,g,b] 0-1  - ambient/fill contribution at that time
angle_pitch   degrees      - sun arc: 0 at horizon (sunrise) -> -90 overhead (midday) ->
-180 (sunset). Yaw/roll are fixed on the light node for v1.
HEIGHT FOG: [fog_height, thickness, noise, distance] keyed by event. THIS IS THE SKY/FOG MATCH:
fog colour is taken from the active celestial light colour, so sky and fog always agree
(docs/20_player_interface/24_world_rendering.md). Mapping to Godot Environment:
fog_height - world Y below which ground fog accumulates (0 = none). Volumetric-fog height term.
thickness  - fog density / opacity                          -> Environment.fog_density
noise      - animated noise breakup strength (cosmetic; defer)
distance   - MAX honest view distance in world units        -> Environment.fog_depth_end
(final cap = min(distance, render budget from doc 06))
STARFIELD: brightness 0 in daylight, 1 at night; drives the star layer / night sky tint.
SKY GRADIENT: if the faithful [time x height] sky-shader route is chosen (08_sky_plan.md Q4),
the per-weather gradient PNG path lives on the weather file, not here. If instead ProceduralSky
colours are driven from data, add a 'sky_gradient_colors' block here keyed to the same events.
ENVIRONMENT (Phase 1): the non-time-varying renderer base + the current static sky look,
mirrored from scenes/main/debug_world.tscn. SkyController applies this on boot, so the look
now lives in data with no visual change. Phase 2 will animate sky_*_color / fog_light_color /
fog_depth_end from the sun + height_fog curves below, keyed to WorldClock.

environment.__note_depth_range: fog_depth_begin/end are NOT static — SkyController pins them to the camera far clip (begin = 0.7 x far) so terrain dissolves into the sky at the draw distance (Stonehearth voxel/fog model).

__comment_sky_gradient_colors: PHASE 2 day/night sky. top / horizon / ground_bottom colours keyed by event name.
SkyController evaluates these against WorldClock.hour each frame and drives the
ProceduralSkyMaterial. fog_light_color tracks 'horizon' so fog always matches the sky.
Hand-authored starting values (midday = the Phase-1 static look); calibrate against screenshots.

__light_color_note: WARM-WHITE values (blue-grass fix, 08_sky_plan.md S1a). SkyController normalises the hue
(rgb / max) and uses the max channel as brightness (energy = max x 1.5), so:
[0.67, 0.65, 0.62] -> hue (1.0, 0.97, 0.93) near-white, energy ~1.0 = the original scene sun.
Do NOT seed these from Stonehearth's bluish light values - their renderer, not ours.
